paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Wisdom is not hiding. She's in the street, in the square, at the city gates, and she is CALLING. Nobody has to climb a mountain or crack a secret code to find her (Proverbs 1:20-21). The trouble in this passage is not that Wisdom is hard to find. It's that people hear her and keep walking.

That's the part that should make us sit up. Wisdom says they refused her call, and "no one took my outstretched hand" (Proverbs 1:24). Then she says they "hated knowledge and chose not to fear the LORD" (Proverbs 1:29). I think that's a warning for all of us, because ignoring good counsel never feels like a big decision. It feels like hitting snooze one more time, and I know that move well.

But look at how she ends. The ones who ignore her "will eat the fruit of their own way" (Proverbs 1:31), but she finishes with a promise: "whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil" (Proverbs 1:33). So here's your takeaway, baker. When God's wisdom calls, today is a good day to listen, and the door is open to anyone who will.
